name: Onyx (formerly Danswer)
licence: NOASSERTION (GitHub could not detect one SPDX licence; custom or mixed, read the repo LICENSE)
what: Self-hosted AI chat and enterprise search with 40+ connectors (Slack, Drive, Confluence, Jira, GitHub and more) and per-user document permissions.
fit: Closest working example of the target: connectors pull docs into its own index, permissions are synced, LLMs query it.
limits: Stores chunk text and embeddings in its own index (a copy of content), and enterprise features sit outside the open core.

name: RAGFlow
what: RAG engine with deep document parsing, agent workflows and data-source sync.
fit: Good parsing and retrieval engine to borrow or embed for the document layer.
limits: Built around ingesting documents into its own store, with weaker per-user ACL than Onyx.

name: Khoj
what: Self-hostable personal AI second brain over your docs and the web, with agents and automations.
fit: Shows a clean chat-over-your-files UX that can be a front end idea.
limits: Personal-scale, not multi-user company ACLs, and AGPL limits embedding in a product.

name: Airweave
what: Open-source context retrieval layer that syncs data from apps and exposes it to agents.
fit: Nearest purpose-built match: connect many apps, keep a synced searchable layer, serve agents.
limits: Smaller project; last push is months old, so check it is still maintained.

name: Supermemory company-brain
what: Open-sourced Slack teammate that remembers what the team says and can go do work.
fit: Reference for a Slack-first brain built on a memory API.
limits: Slack-centric and young; not a multi-source index with ACLs.

name: Agno Scout
what: Open-source company brain built on the Agno agent framework.
fit: Useful pattern for an agent that answers from live sources instead of a big store.
limits: Small; tied to Agno framework.

name: Ankole
what: Self-hosted agent harness with a company brain for Slack, Teams, Lark, DingTalk, WeCom.
fit: Shows chat-channel delivery of a brain, including China-region chat apps.
limits: Very new and small; unproven at scale.

name: Kombo company-brain template
what: Template that syncs company data sources into Git as plain Markdown for coding agents.
fit: Example of the opposite design (full copy as Markdown), useful as a contrast.
limits: Is a copy by design, so it does not meet the index-not-copy rule.

name: Zilobase
what: Open-source self-hostable company brain: notes, databases, AI workflows, context from existing tools.
fit: Watch-list item for a combined workspace plus brain.
limits: Tiny and new.

name: Airbyte
licence: NOASSERTION (GitHub could not detect one SPDX licence; custom or mixed, read the repo LICENSE)
what: Open-source ELT with hundreds of source connectors, now also pitched for AI agents.
fit: Large catalogue of connectors with incremental sync state, usable to feed the index.
limits: Built to land full data in a destination, so you must discard or limit payloads; licence is mixed.

name: Nango
licence: NOASSERTION (GitHub could not detect one SPDX licence; custom or mixed, read the repo LICENSE)
what: Auth, token refresh, API proxy, syncs and webhooks for about 1,000 APIs.
fit: Handles OAuth per user and per tenant plus sync scripts that emit only metadata if you choose.
limits: Licence is not plain open source (check Elastic-style terms); syncs write records to Nango's own cache.

name: Composio
what: 1,000+ agent toolkits with auth, tool search and a sandbox.
fit: Fast way to get live fetch-on-demand tools into an agent without writing each SaaS client.
limits: Tool-calling layer, not an index; hosted backend does much of the auth work.

name: Pipedream
licence: NOASSERTION (GitHub could not detect one SPDX licence; custom or mixed, read the repo LICENSE)
what: Registry of thousands of triggers and actions for SaaS apps, plus a hosted runtime.
fit: Its open component registry gives webhook and polling triggers for change events.
limits: Platform itself is hosted and closed; the open part is the components.

name: Unstructured
what: Open-source ETL to turn PDFs, Office files and web pages into clean text and chunks, with source connectors.
fit: Parser for the moment a file is fetched live or indexed.
limits: Parsing only; no permission model or live sync of its own.

name: LlamaIndex
what: Framework with a large library of data readers and index and query engines.
fit: Readers give quick connectors, and its retrievers can call live tools instead of stored text.
limits: Readers are community quality; no built-in ACL enforcement.

name: Meltano
what: Declarative ELT built on Singer taps, with state for incremental runs.
fit: Mature incremental-sync pattern and hundreds of taps.
limits: Batch oriented and warehouse focused; small community.

name: dlt
what: Python library to load API data with schema handling and incremental state.
fit: Light way to write custom connectors that only record metadata and cursors.
limits: Library, not a service; no search or ACL.

name: Steampipe
what: Query cloud and SaaS APIs live with SQL, no database copy.
fit: Real example of live query with no stored copy, which is the fetch-on-demand half.
limits: Slow for broad scans, API rate limits, AGPL; plugin catalogue is cloud and dev heavy.

name: CocoIndex
what: Incremental indexing engine that re-processes only what changed, from sources to vector and graph targets.
fit: Fits the self-updating index: change detection and lineage are the core feature.
limits: Young; connector list is smaller than Airbyte.

name: Pathway
licence: NOASSERTION (GitHub could not detect one SPDX licence; custom or mixed, read the repo LICENSE)
what: Streaming ETL framework with live document indexing for RAG.
fit: Keeps a vector index updated as source files change.
limits: Source-available licence (BSL-style); check terms before use.

name: Activepieces
licence: NOASSERTION (GitHub could not detect one SPDX licence; custom or mixed, read the repo LICENSE)
what: Open workflow automation with about 400 pieces that also act as MCP servers.
fit: Cheap source of app triggers and MCP exposure for many SaaS apps.
limits: Enterprise features are under a separate licence; not an index.

name: n8n
licence: NOASSERTION (GitHub could not detect one SPDX licence; custom or mixed, read the repo LICENSE)
what: Fair-code workflow automation with 400+ integrations and AI nodes.
fit: Handy glue for webhooks and low-volume sync jobs.
limits: Sustainable-use licence restricts reselling; not built for index or ACL work.

name: MCP reference servers
licence: NOASSERTION (GitHub could not detect one SPDX licence; custom or mixed, read the repo LICENSE)
what: Official collection of reference MCP servers (filesystem, git, fetch, memory and others).
fit: Pattern for exposing each app as live tools the LLM calls on demand.
limits: Reference quality; many vendor-grade SaaS servers live elsewhere.

name: MCP Registry
licence: NOASSERTION (GitHub could not detect one SPDX licence; custom or mixed, read the repo LICENSE)
what: Community registry service for discovering MCP servers.
fit: Source of truth for finding and pinning vendor MCP servers per app.
limits: Metadata only; says nothing about server safety.

name: IBM MCP Context Forge
what: Gateway, registry and proxy in front of MCP, A2A and REST tools with guardrails.
fit: One front door for all app tools with central policy and logging.
limits: Large and fast-moving; you operate it yourself.

name: Docker MCP Gateway
what: Docker CLI plugin that runs MCP servers in containers behind one gateway.
fit: Isolates each connector in a container.
limits: Developer-desktop focus, light on enterprise identity.

name: agentgateway
what: Proxy for agent, LLM and MCP traffic with auth and policy.
fit: Policy point where per-user tokens and tool allow-lists can be enforced.
limits: Proxy only; you bring the connectors.

name: MCP Gateway & Registry
what: Gateway plus registry with OAuth and dynamic tool discovery.
fit: Dynamic tool discovery helps when a company has hundreds of app tools.
limits: Small community.

name: Metorial
licence: NOASSERTION (GitHub could not detect one SPDX licence; custom or mixed, read the repo LICENSE)
what: Connect any model to 1,200+ integrations over MCP, CLI or API.
fit: Alternative hosted-or-self-host source of MCP connectors.
limits: Licence is not a clear SPDX; check terms.

name: FastMCP
what: Python framework for building MCP servers and clients.
fit: Fastest way to wrap the brain's own search as an MCP server.
limits: Framework only.

name: Letta
what: Platform for stateful agents with self-editing memory.
fit: Memory for the agent's own learned facts, kept apart from company documents.
limits: Agent-centric, not a document index.

name: Mem0
what: Memory layer that extracts and retrieves facts per user or agent.
fit: Per-person preferences and facts without storing source documents.
limits: Memory of conversations, not enterprise ACL-aware.

name: Graphiti (Zep)
what: Temporal knowledge graph that updates in real time as facts change.
fit: Stores entities and pointers with validity times, a good shape for a company map that points to sources.
limits: Needs a graph database and LLM calls on every ingest, which costs money.

name: Cognee
what: Open-source AI memory platform that builds graph plus vector memory.
fit: Option for a graph layer over extracted entities.
limits: Ingest-heavy; ACLs are limited.

name: Supermemory
what: Memory and context engine, runnable fully locally.
fit: Another memory API with connectors to a few apps.
limits: Product-style memory; not full enterprise permissions.

name: Vespa
what: Search platform doing hybrid text, vector and ranking with per-query filters at large scale.
fit: Strong choice for the core index: hybrid ranking and ACL filters in one query.
limits: Heavier to run than a single-node engine.

name: Qdrant
what: Rust vector database with payload filtering and hybrid support.
fit: Light, fast store for pointer records plus ACL payload filters.
limits: Keyword search is weaker than Elasticsearch or Vespa.

name: Weaviate
licence: NOASSERTION (GitHub could not detect one SPDX licence; custom or mixed, read the repo LICENSE)
what: Vector database with hybrid search and multi-tenancy.
fit: Per-tenant isolation fits company or client separation.
limits: GitHub shows no single licence, so confirm terms.

name: Milvus
what: Cloud-native vector database built for very large ANN search.
fit: Fits if index grows to billions of chunks.
limits: Many moving parts to operate.

name: pgvector
licence: NOASSERTION (GitHub could not detect one SPDX licence; custom or mixed, read the repo LICENSE)
what: Postgres extension for vector similarity (PostgreSQL-style licence).
fit: Simplest start: pointers, metadata, ACL rows and vectors in one Postgres with real joins.
limits: Slower than dedicated engines at very large scale.

name: pgvectorscale
what: DiskANN-style index extension that scales pgvector.
fit: Extends the Postgres-only plan further before needing a new engine.
limits: Tied to Postgres, smaller community.

name: OpenSearch
what: Apache-licensed search engine with keyword, vector and hybrid, plus document-level security.
fit: Document-level security plugin gives a ready ACL filter.
limits: Operationally heavy.

name: Elasticsearch
licence: NOASSERTION (GitHub could not detect one SPDX licence; custom or mixed, read the repo LICENSE)
what: Industry-standard search engine with hybrid and vector search.
fit: Mature option if the team already runs it.
limits: Licence is multi (Elastic and AGPL options); read before shipping to customers.

name: LanceDB
what: Embedded vector and full-text store on object storage.
fit: Cheap, per-tenant indexes kept on S3.
limits: Less tested for heavy concurrent multi-user ACL queries.

name: Vald
what: Distributed vector search engine on Kubernetes.
fit: Option for a pure vector tier.
limits: Small community; vectors only, no keyword.

name: Haystack
what: Pipeline framework for RAG and agents.
fit: Clean pipelines where a retriever is a swappable live-fetch or index lookup.
limits: No ACL or connector sync of its own.

name: LightRAG
what: Light graph-based RAG with incremental updates.
fit: Incremental graph updates are cheaper than full GraphRAG rebuilds.
limits: Quality depends on the extraction model; no ACL.

name: Microsoft GraphRAG
what: Modular graph-based RAG from Microsoft Research.
fit: Good for broad whole-company questions.
limits: Expensive to build and re-run on change; research code.

name: R2R (SciPhi)
what: Agentic RAG system with a REST API.
fit: Reference API shape for a retrieval service.
limits: No push since Nov 2025, so treat as stale.

name: OpenFGA
what: Zanzibar-style relationship-based authorization engine (CNCF).
fit: Model Drive folder, Slack channel and Jira project access as relations and filter results per user.
limits: You must sync permissions from each app yourself.

name: SpiceDB
what: Zanzibar-inspired permissions database with a lookup-resources API.
fit: Its list-what-this-user-can-see call suits pre-filtering search results.
limits: Same permission-sync work; schema design is hard.

name: Cerbos
what: Policy-based authorization service, now also for AI agents.
fit: Good for policy rules like sensitivity labels on top of source ACLs.
limits: Policy engine, not a relationship store.

name: Open Policy Agent
what: General-purpose policy engine (CNCF graduated).
fit: Gate agent actions and tool calls with one policy language.
limits: Not built for per-document relation lookups at scale.

name: Debezium
what: Change data capture for databases into Kafka-style streams.
fit: Captures changes from company databases without polling.
limits: Databases only, not SaaS APIs; needs Kafka or similar.

name: Temporal
what: Durable workflow engine with retries and long-running state.
fit: Runs resumable sync, backfill and webhook-reconcile jobs that survive failures and rate limits.
limits: Another cluster to run; you write the workflows.

name: Docling
what: Document conversion to structured text for gen AI.
fit: Parser for fetched files, strong on layout and tables.
limits: Parsing only.
